**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated August 14, 2026**
**Member:** Harper Alvarez | **Member ID:** W950863136
**Reference number:** POC-0FFFC72471-45570
**Service denied:** Neck (cervical) fusion (ACDF), CPT 22551
**Governing policy:** Aetna CPB 0743 – Spinal Surgery: Laminectomy and Fusion (https://www.aetna.com/cpb/medical/data/700_799/0743.html)

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for the cervical fusion (ACDF, CPT 22551) requested by my surgeon, Dr. Reyes, MD. The notice dated August 14, 2026 states that the documentation submitted was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity. I am asking Aetna to reconsider that decision, because the records in my chart do address each of the criteria in the plan's own policy. If something specific was missing, I am asking the plan to tell me exactly what it was so I can supply it.

Below I have set out the plan's published criteria in its own words, followed by what my records show.

---

**1. Conservative therapy**

The policy states:

> "Member has failed at least 6 weeks of conservative therapy Footnote1 * (unless there is an indication for waiver of requirements for conservative management, noted below); and"

> "Conservative measures must be recent (within the past year) and include the following non-surgical measures and medications unless one or more of the requirements for waiver below are met: patient education; active physical therapy (in-person as opposed to home or virtual physical therapy); medications (NSAIDS, acetaminophen, or tricyclic antidepressants), and (where appropriate) identification and management of associated anxiety and depression."

> "The member should participate in physical therapy for the entire required duration of conservative management (six weeks or three months, depending upon the indication for surgery). Physical therapy needs to be confirmed either by the actual PT notes, or by documentation in the member claims history."

My records show supervised, in-person physical therapy including cervical traction and postural training for 8 weeks, from April 27, 2026 to June 22, 2026, with 20 visits completed. This is documented in the physical therapy discharge note, which is the type of confirmation the policy asks for. My records also document NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief, and a corticosteroid injection on April 1, 2026 that gave only about two weeks of partial relief. All of this care occurred within the past year. My symptoms have continued for 18 months and are progressive, and are not relieved by rest.

If the physical therapy notes did not reach the reviewer, I am asking that they be requested from my treating providers and that the claims history for those 20 visits be checked, as the policy allows.

**2. Waiver provision**

The policy also states:

> "The requirement for a trial of conservative measures may be waived in the following situations indicating need for urgent intervention: Spinal cord compression (this does not include nerve root compression); Stenosis causing cauda equina syndrome; Stenosis causing myelopathy (only applicable for cervical and thoracic spine cases, not lumbar)"

I am not relying on a waiver. I am pointing to this language only to show that I completed the full course of conservative care the policy expects rather than seeking an exception to it.

**3. Signs or symptoms of neural compression at the levels being treated**

The policy states:

> "Member has signs or symptoms of neural compression (radiculopathy, neurogenic claudication, myelopathy) associated with the levels being treated; and"

My records document radicular pain and numbness into my right thumb and index finger, with weakness. My examination documents positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level.

**4. Advanced imaging at the corresponding level**

The policy states:

> "Advanced imaging studies (CT or MRI) indicate central/lateral recess or foraminal stenosis (graded as moderate, moderate to severe or severe; not mild or mild to moderate), or nerve root or spinal cord compression, at the level corresponding with the clinical findings; and"

> "Advanced imaging studies are required prior to any spinal surgery. The imaging should be performed within the past year, or after the onset of the current constellation of symptoms or any relevant surgical procedures, whichever is sooner."

An MRI of my cervical spine dated July 13, 2026 shows a C5-C6 disc herniation with **severe** right foraminal narrowing and **C6 nerve root compression**. That study is recent, it is within the past year, and the findings are on the same side and at the same level as my symptoms and examination findings.

**5. Other sources of pain ruled out**

The policy states:

> "All other reasonable sources of pain and/or neurological deficit have been ruled out, including but not limited to significant pathology at other spinal level(s) on the advanced imaging radiology report that is/are not part of the surgical request resulting in incomplete surgical planning; and"

The MRI report of July 13, 2026 identifies the C5-C6 level as the source of the nerve root compression, and that is the level for which surgery has been requested. My symptoms and examination findings point to the same level. If the reviewer believes the radiology report describes additional pathology that makes the surgical plan incomplete, I ask that the specific finding be identified in writing so my surgeon can address it directly.

**6. Examination by the operating surgeon**

The policy states:

> "Medical records must document that a physical examination, including a neurologic examination, has been performed by or reviewed by the operating surgeon."

My records include physical examination findings, including neurologic findings, and my operating surgeon is Dr. Reyes, MD, of orthopedic surgery. I am asking that Dr. Reyes's examination note of [date of Dr. Reyes's examination note] be reviewed as part of this appeal; my surgeon has documented that this procedure is needed.

**7. Nicotine**

The policy states:

> "Member should be nicotine-free (including smoking, use of tobacco products, and nicotine replacement therapy) for at least 6 weeks prior to surgery."

> "For persons with recent (within a year) nicotine use (unless there is an indication (e.g., myelopathy, cauda equina syndrome), severe weakness (graded 4 minus or less on MRC scale) or progressive weakness, or an associated infection/tumor and/or fracture), documentation of nicotine cessation should include a lab report (not surgeon summary) showing blood and/or urine nicotine level of less than or equal to 10 ng/ml (or urinary cotinine levels of less than or equal to 10 ng/ml), drawn within 6 weeks prior to surgery;"

My records document that I am a non-smoker. The lab-report provision above applies to persons with recent nicotine use, and my records do not document recent nicotine use.

**8. Activities of daily living**

The policy states:

> "Member's activities of daily living are limited by symptoms of neural compression;"

My records document 18 months of progressive neck pain that is not relieved by rest, along with radicular pain, numbness in my right thumb and index finger, and weakness. I am including a short personal statement describing how these symptoms limit my day-to-day activities: [brief description of the specific daily activities I can no longer do].

---

**A note on what I have been able to quote**

The excerpts above are the plan's own published language from Aetna CPB 0743. I want to be straightforward that the policy contains further conditions and lists that I have not reproduced here, including the footnoted conservative-therapy provision, because I do not have that text in front of me. My records also do not address diabetes or hemoglobin A1C, and I have not been told that the plan's A1C provision was applied to me.

Because the stated reason for denial is incomplete documentation rather than a specific clinical finding, I am asking the plan to identify, in writing, which criterion or criteria in CPB 0743 it applied and exactly which document it found missing. If a record is missing from the file, I will obtain it and submit it promptly.

---

**What I am asking for**

I respectfully ask that Aetna:

1. Overturn the denial dated August 14, 2026 (reference POC-0FFFC72471-45570) and authorize CPT 22551; or
2. If the denial is maintained, state in writing the specific criterion from Aetna CPB 0743 that was not met and the specific document that was found missing, so it can be supplied.

I am submitting this appeal on the Aetna Member Complaint and Appeal Form (available in my account at aetna.com under complaints, grievances and appeals), sent to the appeal address printed on my denial letter, or by fax to 859-425-3379. My denial notice states that my appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the notice, by **February 10, 2027**. I understand I may also call 1-800-872-3862 or the number on my member ID card with questions about this appeal.

Documents I am enclosing:

- Physical therapy discharge note covering 20 visits, April 27, 2026 – June 22, 2026
- Cervical spine MRI report dated July 13, 2026
- Office and examination notes from Dr. Reyes, MD
- Medication history and record of the April 1, 2026 corticosteroid injection
- A copy of the denial notice dated August 14, 2026
- [Any additional records I am attaching]

Thank you for taking a fresh look at this. I would appreciate a written decision as soon as the plan is able to provide one.

Sincerely,

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_
Harper Alvarez
